paper_title: What are they talking about Benchmarking Large Language Models for   Knowledge-Grounded Discussion Summarization
caption: Expert win rates 0.90\% in EBS feedback judgment. Our annotations achieve an average win rate of 88.890.90\%. All 12 LLMs exceed an 820.90\% rate in preferring our EBS.
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates expert win rates (in percent) for an “EBS feedback judgment” across an overall average and a set of named large language models. The horizontal axis contains the categories (model names), shown as diagonally rotated labels in the following displayed order: Average, GPT-4o, GPT-4-turbo, GPT-4o-mini, Claude 3 Opus, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Claude 3.5 Haiku, Gemini 1.5 Pro, Llama-3.1-405B, Mistral Large, DeepSeek V3, Qwen2-Max, and GLM-4-Plus. The vertical axis is labeled “Expert Win Rate (%)” and uses a linear scale from 0 to 110, with regularly spaced tick marks every 20 units (0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100). Each category is represented by a single solid-colored bar (no stacking or grouping) with a numeric value printed above it: Average is a dark gray bar at 88.89; GPT-4o is a muted teal bar at 84.38; GPT-4-turbo is a lavender bar at 91.67; GPT-4o-mini is a blue bar at 97.56; Claude 3 Opus is a mauve/pink bar at 83.12; Claude 3.5 Sonnet is a light steel-blue bar at 88.46; Claude 3.5 Haiku is a tan/brown bar at 86.25; Gemini 1.5 Pro is a light blue bar at 87.04; Llama-3.1-405B is a pale purple bar at 97.14; Mistral Large is a beige bar at 91.14; DeepSeek V3 is a light gray bar at 82.26; Qwen2-Max is a pale cream bar at 85.07; and GLM-4-Plus is a very light pink bar at 92.54. The bars are presented in the listed sequence rather than being visually sorted by height, and there is no legend or additional visual emphasis beyond the value annotations above each bar.
